claims.text: Adding a small amount of Sc or Y to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Adding Sc or Y will preserve the room-temperature mechanical performance of HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding Sc or Y will preserve the high-temperature mechanical performance of HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y addition will produce a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The added Sc or Y atoms will occupy lattice sites in HfMoTaTiZr.
Substitution by Sc or Y on lattice sites will reduce the alloy's overall density.
Sc or Y addition will maintain a high-entropy, single-phase microstructure.
Maintaining the high-entropy, single-phase microstructure will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will have a density below 9.5 g cm−3.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The relevant loading condition is uniaxial tension from room temperature to 1600 °C.
The hypothesis is to be rejected unless density decreases by at least 5% while the alloy maintains yield strengths above 1500 MPa at room temperature and 800 MPa at 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted density target is below 9.5 g cm−3, whereas a 5% reduction from the 10.21 g cm−3 baseline only requires density below approximately 9.70 g cm−3. Thus, an outcome between 9.5 and 9.70 g cm−3 would fail the stated prediction but pass the falsification threshold.

The hypothesis says performance will not be sacrificed, but the room-temperature acceptance threshold permits yield strength to decline from 1600 MPa to just above 1500 MPa. The high-temperature threshold similarly permits a decline relative to 855 MPa, although the baseline temperature for that value is not specified.
